'''Wilfred Gordon Malcolm''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|size=100%|CBE}} (29 November 1933 – 6 October 2018) was a New Zealand mathematician and university administrator. He was professor of [[pure mathematics]] at [[Victoria University of Wellington]] from the mid 1970s, until serving as vice-chancellor of the [[University of Waikato]] between 1985 and 1994.

==Biography==
Born in [[Feilding]] on 29 November 1933, Malcolm was educated at [[Feilding Agricultural High School]]. He went on to study at [[Wellington Teachers' College]] and [[Victoria University College]], graduating [[Master of Arts]] with first-class honours in 1957.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university15.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Ma |website=Shadows of Time |accessdate=9 October 2018}}</ref><ref name="NZMS">{{cite news | url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/downloads/profiles/NZMSprofile33_Wilf_Malcolm.pdf | title=Professor Wilf Malcolm | date=April 1985 | work=NZMS Newsletter | issue=33 | accessdate=9 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Malcolm |first=Wilfred |year=1972 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Ultraproducts and Higher Order Models |publisher=Open Access Repository Victoria University of Wellington, Victoria University of Wellington |doi=10.26686/wgtn.16958536|doi-access=free |url=https://figshare.com/articles/thesis/Ultraproducts_and_Higher_Order_Models/16958536/1/files/31373422.pdf }}</ref> He won a Shirtcliffe Fellowship, which enabled him to take parts II and III of the [[Mathematical Tripos]], specialising in algebra and topology, at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="NZMS"/> While in England, Malcolm married Edmée Ruth Prebensen.<ref name="NZMS"/>

Malcolm returned to Victoria, where he took up a lecturership in pure mathematics.<ref name="NZMS"/> Between 1964 and 1966, he spent time away from the university, working as the general secretary of the [[Tertiary Students Christian Fellowship|Inter-Varsity Fellowship of Evangelical Unions]].<ref name="NZMS"/> However, he returned to lecturing at Victoria in 1967, and was promoted to senior lecturer the following year.<ref name="NZMS"/> In 1972, he completed his [[PhD]] thesis, titled ''Ultraproducts and higher order models'', supervised by [[George Edward Hughes|George Hughes]] and [[Max Cresswell]] from the Department of Philosophy, and C.J. Seelye from the Mathematics Department.<ref name="NZMS"/><ref>{{CiteQ|Q111966094|type=Doctoral thesis}}</ref>

In 1985, Malcolm moved to the University of Waikato to take up the vice-chancellorship, serving in that role until 1994.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://calendar.waikato.ac.nz/officershonoursstaff/vicechancellors.html | title=Former vice-chancellors of the University of Waikato | publisher=University of Waikato | accessdate=9 October 2018}}</ref>

Malcolm was awarded the [[New Zealand 1990 Commemoration Medal]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Taylor |first1=Alister |last2=Coddington |first2=Deborah |author-link1=Alister Taylor |author-link2=Deborah Coddington |title=Honoured by the Queen – New Zealand |year=1994 |publisher=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa |location=Auckland |isbn=0-908578-34-2 |page=239}}</ref> In the [[1994 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|1994 Queen's Birthday Honours]], he was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]], for services to tertiary education.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=53697 |date=11 June 1994 |page=34 |supp=2}}</ref> The following year, he was conferred with an honorary doctorate by the University of Waikato.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://calendar.waikato.ac.nz/officershonoursstaff/doctors.html | title=Honorary doctors of the University of Waikato | publisher=University of Waikato | accessdate=9 October 2018 | archive-date=6 April 2001 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010406115418/http://calendar.waikato.ac.nz/officershonoursstaff/doctors.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> The Wilf Malcolm Institute of Educational Research at Waikato was named in his honour in 2002, in recognition of his contribution to education.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gaps.net.nz/academy-and-christ |title=Academy and learning |website=Art in the Gaps |accessdate=9 October 2018}}</ref>

Malcolm died in Auckland on 6 October 2018.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://notices.nzherald.co.nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/obituary.aspx?n=wilfred-gordon-obe-malcolm-wilf&pid=190414855 | title=Wilfred Gordon Malcolm death notice | date=8 October 2018 | work=New Zealand Herald | accessdate=9 October 2018}}</ref>
